lessons.title: Methods of separation
lessons.programRef: Form 3 Chemistry — Separation methods (to be checked)

lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Describe filtration, evaporation, crystallisation, simple and fractional distillation, chromatography and use of a separating funnel.
Choose the correct method for a mixture.
Calculate Rf values and describe how melting and boiling points show purity.
reviewNotes: Fractional distillation is mentioned at an introductory level; check the Form 3 syllabus. Safety: heating flammable liquids to be done by the teacher.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Choosing a method
blocks.md:
- **Filtration**: insoluble solid from a liquid (sand from water). The solid is the **residue**, the liquid the **filtrate**.
- **Evaporation / crystallisation**: dissolved solid from a solution (salt from sea water; salt pans at the coast).
- **Simple distillation**: pure solvent from a solution (pure water).
- **Fractional distillation**: liquids with different boiling points (ethanol and water; crude oil).
- **Separating funnel**: immiscible liquids (oil and water).
- **Magnet**: iron from other solids. **Sublimation**: iodine or ammonium chloride from sand.

blocks.caption: Simple distillation of a solution.
blocks.alt: A flask with a thermometer and heat on the left, a slanting condenser with cold water going in at the lower end and out at the upper end, and a beaker collecting pure liquid on the right.

blocks.title: Chromatography and purity
blocks.md: In **paper chromatography** a spot of the mixture is placed above the solvent on the start line; the solvent rises and carries the substances by different distances. **Rf = distance moved by the substance ÷ distance moved by the solvent front**. The same substance always gives the same Rf in the same solvent. A **pure** substance has a **sharp** melting or boiling point; an impure one melts over a range and at a lower temperature, boils at a higher temperature.

blocks.caption: A chromatogram: the mixture contains two dyes, as shown by comparing with dye 1 and dye 2.
blocks.alt: A paper strip with a start line and solvent front; the mixture column has two spots matching the single spots of dye 1 and dye 2.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Filtration cannot separate a dissolved solid: use evaporation or crystallisation.
- The start line of a chromatogram is drawn in **pencil** (pencil does not dissolve) and kept **above** the solvent.
- Distillation uses a thermometer at the top of the flask near the side arm: it reads the boiling point of the vapour.

blocks.title: Rf value
blocks.statement: In a chromatogram the solvent front moved 6.0 cm and a dye spot moved 3.6 cm. Find its Rf.

blocks.title: Separate salt and sand
blocks.statement: Describe how to obtain dry sand and dry salt from a mixture.
steps: Add water, stir to dissolve the salt, then filter; wash and dry the residue (sand).
Heat the filtrate in an evaporating dish until crystals form and dry them (salt).
